system.name: EDM
system.one_liner: an ultra-low latency Ethernet fabric for memory disaggregation implemented within the Ethernet PHY

content.key_idea: Replacing the intra-server processor-memory interconnect with an Ethernet fabric turns remote memory access into a NIC-to-switch-to-NIC path through PHY-level stacks, which is the paper's focus.
content.reading_order: Top shows the baseline intra-server processor-to-memory path; a 'V.S.' divider separates it from the bottom Ethernet-based Compute Node/Memory Node architecture, read left to right through NIC, switch, NIC.

evidence: Memory disaggregation is a computing architecture in which compute and memory are physically separate nodes
Using Ethernet as the interconnect between the processor and the memory introduces two sources of latency
the processor/memory to NIC interconnect latency, and (ii) the Ethernet fabric latency

summary: EDM targets memory disaggregation over Ethernet, where compute and memory live on separate nodes connected by a network fabric. This figure contrasts the traditional intra-server processor-to-memory interconnect (top) with an Ethernet-based Compute Node/Memory Node architecture (bottom), separated by a 'V.S.' divider. Each node contains a processor or DRAM plus a NIC holding a network protocol stack (e.g., RDMA), an Ethernet MAC, and an Ethernet PHY; the two nodes connect through an Ethernet Switch that also has MAC/PHY layers and a Layer 2 forwarding pipeline. Dashed orange labels mark the 'Ethernet Fabric (focus of this paper)', spanning NIC PHYs and the switch, motivating why EDM targets the PHY layer to cut remote memory access latency instead of the traditional MAC-layer protocol stack.
